contract.input: ONLY policy.input is model-visible; action and weight are supervised labels. Never train on *_challenge_EVALUATOR_ONLY.jsonl.
contract.world_group: Group by (source_split,source_world_index,source_seed,geometry_sha256), and explicitly compare geometry hashes across all v44-v50 releases. v50 source-world indices start at 200 and are not used by v46-v49.
contract.drift: Physical host flips the contextual material mapping at first arrival at an objective without issuing a change event. Teacher cannot see flip; it initially issues the previously calibrated command, reads physical outcome, erases wrong material and corrects using that new observation.
contract.leakage: No hidden drift flags or host laws are in model input. Episode-labelled world / arm / expected material / error counts occur only in evaluator metadata.
contract.dedup: TRAIN exact repeated inputs and movement records that differ only by irrelevant A/B physical receipts are zero-weighted. DEV/HELDOUT retained unsampled.
contract.labels: Every trajectory action was legal and host accepted; PAINT_RESULT is generated only after actual synthetic accepted paint, not an oracle tool-law signal.

limitations: Synthetic graph/material game-like host, not native CyberSand
Pre-mission calibration and early survey remain scripted host operations
Binary contextual tool laws permit symbolic inference; model training and actual transfer remain unevaluated
Unannounced mid-objective drift is synthetic; native game semantics require separate validation
A simple online receipt parser can still solve recovery; this is a discriminative DATA challenge, not learned behavior
No LFM/Sprocket training or neural latency/RSS; dataset not in immutable Actions artifacts
